name: Pinch
description:
A jointed arm swinging in and its claw shutting. Spider Hand was silent; the first version of this gave it a voice made of noise — a band sweeping up for the swing, two noise clicks for the snap — and up to eight arms of that in a second was a fistful of static.

A claw closing is a knock, not a hiss, so the snap is struck now, the way a woodblock is. `clack` is the first half of the pincer meeting: a sine at `$grit` gone in twenty-five milliseconds, with `bite` a hair later at `$gust`, the second half landing a little higher. `partial` is one short sine at `$gust.up` over them — not in any scale, which is what makes the knock read as shell rather than as a note. `swing` is all that is left of the noise: thirty milliseconds under a lowpass, dark and faint, so the bite is announced without the announcement being the loud part. Nothing low: a claw is small, and the hit the bite lands is already the weight.

Ships three takes and sits low, because eight arms can bite inside the same second.
